title: REINS: A Self-Evolving Agent Harness for Real-Time Trajectory Planning
why: A-type self-evolving agent harness for real-time trajectory planning: an LLM planner is wrapped with dynamics grounding, calibrated predicate/rollout verification, and indexed rule memory so novel scenes invoke the LLM while familiar scenes are served from memory without re-invocation.
mechanism: REINS runtime harness with three LLM-planner couplings: outputs are grounded to a learned variable-level dynamics model, verified via calibrated predicates and forward rollout, and consolidated into an indexed rule memory served in O(log n) without re-invoking the LLM. Familiar scenes resolve by memory lookup; novel scenes invoke the LLM and verified outputs enrich the memory. LLM weights are not modified.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): 98%+ compliance, nearly 50% collision reduction, and 1.9-4.6 ms latency on simulated and real-world benchmarks at the tactical decision layer, with LLM invocation rate monotonically declining as memory matures.

title: Embodied First Exam
why: B-type agent-native benchmark for coding agents that control diverse robots: agents may choose direct control, code-to-control, or train-a-policy-to-control, under Standard (sensor-only, no reset), Realtime, and Privileged settings.
mechanism: Embodied First Exam: 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites beyond pick-and-place (spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering). Coding agents choose their control approach. The Standard Setting provides only sensor observations and, by default, disallows environment resets; a Realtime variant keeps the environment running while the agent reasons; the Privileged Setting exposes full simulator state and unlimited resets so the agent can search for an oracle solution. Failures are labeled by the stage at which attempts go wrong.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on the 456 core tasks, the strongest of eight agents, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, achieves a 34% success rate in the Standard Setting; Privileged-setting success is described as an approximate upper bound (numeric tables beyond abstract unread).

title: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary
why: B-type safety benchmark (ArmedAgent) for coding agents that control a real robot arm zero-shot: evaluates robustness, capability misuse, and digital-to-physical transfer of threats such as indirect prompt injection.
mechanism: ArmedAgent benchmark for coding agents performing zero-shot, end-to-end robot-arm control without task-specific demonstrations or retraining. It covers robustness, malicious use, and indirect injection across 36 tasks in 5 scenarios, in simulation and on a physical robot arm. A distinctive subset targets harmful behaviors that earlier VLA/WAM paradigms could not perform, including threats that enter via digital resources (web pages, emails) and can carry over into the physical world.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): several frontier models, including GPT-6-Astra, are tested under widely used agent frameworks and are reported to exhibit substantial safety risks in current systems (numeric tables beyond abstract unread).

title: ReSkill: Selective Self-Improvement for Robot Manipulation
why: A-type coding-agent self-improvement loop for compositional manipulation: the agent builds an object-centric task graph over a skill library, locates failures from execution records, revises stages and skills, and adopts only validated changes; the deployed policy then runs the retained skills without the agent.
mechanism: ReSkill: a coding agent constructs an object-centric task graph from an instruction and a skill library, then uses node-level execution records to locate failures. Task-level revisions cover stage organization, hand-off conditions, and recovery routes; skill-level revisions strengthen perception, motion, manipulation, and verification capabilities that repeatedly fail. Candidate revisions undergo full-task evaluation and paired comparisons before adoption. The agent participates only during development; the deployed policy calls retained skills without invoking the agent at run time.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on the same development set, average success across ten RoboDojo tasks rises from 30.0% for the initial versions to 86.2% for the final adopted programs; retained programs achieve 83.6% in recorded robustness and model-selection evaluations. Across eight real-world tasks, ReSkill succeeds in 72 of 80 rebuilt-simulation trials and 62 of 80 real-robot trials (77.5%). The median revision changes only three functions, approximately 0.5% of a program, while 39% of task-specific functions in later-added tasks directly reuse existing implementations.

title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
why: A-type world-in-the-loop ICL harness for agentic manipulation: a frozen model starts from one demonstration, rehearses the task in a world (e.g. a simulator), writes feedback into context as Task Memory, and deploys that frozen memory on new scenes without gradient updates.
mechanism: World In-Context Learning (WICL): a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. RoboScript implements WICL for agentic manipulation: from a single demonstration it learns each task through rehearsal, freezes the knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation so every deployment input is available on a real robot. The method is reported to improve through reflection and to transfer to a physical dual-arm robot via cross-embodiment memory adaptation.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. Transfer to a physical dual-arm robot is reported (numeric real-robot tables beyond abstract unread).

title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
why: A-type memory-evolution harness for embodied MLLM agents under direct control: the model writes a coordinate-free task memory from one demonstration and refines a bounded working memory from training-episode lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery, with both memories frozen at test time and no weight updates.
mechanism: SimplEvo: an MLLM under direct control retains execution experience in self-written text memories, with no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. It writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration, then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. Working memory written by GPT-6-Astra is reported to be reusable as-is by weaker MLLMs.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Text memory alone is reported to reach a similar SR to memories that also store past visual frames, while using fewer tokens. Fixed memories are also reported to generalize to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations.

title: Flip Anything with Agentic Robotics Self-Learning
why: A-type coding-agent self-learning loop for bimanual object flipping: the agent iteratively develops and refines strategies in physics simulation across object geometries, then deploys graph-based code that combines high-level strategy selection with reactive control on physical robots.
mechanism: A coding agent autonomously develops and refines object-flipping strategies through iterative learning in physics simulations across diverse object geometries. Skill acquisition is progressive: basic handover, toppling and pushing, robust grasping and sensing, and thin-object manipulation with recovery. The resulting graph-based code integrates high-level strategy selection with reactive control for multi-stage flipping on physical robots.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): progressive skill acquisition improves task success from 24.7% to 95.0%. Multi-stage flipping on physical robots is reported (numeric real-robot tables beyond abstract unread).

title: Zero-Shot VLA Adaptation with Retrieved Guidance
why: A-type retrieval harness for a frozen VLA: RAGu geometrically calibrates in-the-wild demonstrations (e.g. DROID), retrieves a compatible trajectory, and guides the base VLA's flow-matching inference without retraining or expanding the context window.
mechanism: RAGu retrieval-augmented guidance for VLAs under domain shift (camera, background, object identity, or morphology). It (1) applies geometric calibration to transform source demonstrations into the target setup, (2) uses coarse-to-fine retrieval over a pool of pre-warped candidates to select the trajectory most compatible with the base VLA, and (3) guides the VLA's flow-matching inference rather than retraining the base model or expanding its context window. Evaluated in real-world, simulation, sim-to-real, and cross-embodiment humanoid manipulation.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): RAGu improves real-world VLA success rates from 20% to 80% and outperforms the closest-related baselines in simulation (numeric tables beyond abstract unread).

title: Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation
why: A-type zero-shot vision-language planning harness for bimanual humanoid manipulation: planning is grounded in a structured scene representation with execution constraints, actions are staged with pre-/post-conditions, and a hierarchical validator uses stage-level history for local recovery or targeted replanning.
mechanism: Zero-shot vision-language framework for execution-aware bimanual manipulation. Planning is grounded in a structured scene representation that combines semantic object relations with execution constraints, used to select obstacle relocations and execution choices while preserving task semantics. Compatible actions are organised into parallel bimanual stages with explicit pre- and post-conditions. A hierarchical validator evaluates these conditions under perceptual uncertainty and uses stage-level execution history to support local recovery or targeted replanning.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): experiments on the CENTAURO hybrid wheeled-legged humanoid across nine language-conditioned manipulation scenarios show higher task success than a non-execution-aware baseline. In dedicated failure scenarios, hierarchical validation recovers from execution failures with fewer model queries than always replanning (numeric tables beyond abstract unread).

title: Streaming Failure Forecasting: VLA Failure Monitors That Keep Learning After Deployment
why: B-type post-deployment success/failure monitor for VLAs: the monitor keeps learning from each episode's success label by refitting only its last linear layer, so it can track unannounced task or policy-version drift instead of remaining frozen.
mechanism: Streaming Failure Forecasting (SFF): a deployed VLA failure monitor keeps the offline network fixed and refits only its last linear layer after each episode from the episode success label (reported 2.18 ms per policy call on a Jetson CPU core). The alarm threshold moves only after successes. The monitor is evaluated under unannounced drift of lighting/objects/cameras and under switches of task or policy version, compared with a frozen monitor and with resetting on detected drift.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): with every setting locked before testing, SFF ranks failures better than the same monitor kept frozen on 4 of 5 simulated test suites under unannounced drift, and above resetting on detected drift on every suite. Carried with locked learner settings to 434 recorded runs of four VLAs on real SO-101 arms, replayed across unannounced switches of task or policy version, it ranks failures better than the frozen monitor for every VLA and, in an exploratory comparison, above a full reset at the true switch.

title: MoE-DAgger: Transition-Aware Router-Entropy Gating for Selective Human Correction in Phase-Structured Manipulation
why: A-type on-policy correction method: selective DAgger for phase-structured manipulation uses causal MoE router history to request human correction only when entropy indicates a stalled, timed-out, or backward phase transition, rather than at normal adjacent handoffs.
mechanism: MoE-DAgger: selective Dataset Aggregation that uses causal router history from a phase-supervised soft mixture-of-experts to distinguish normal adjacent-phase handoffs from persistent or backward routing, without giving the policy a phase label, progress variable, or hard phase command at execution. The acquisition rule allows an adjacent transition to settle, but requests correction when high entropy persists outside such a transition, the transition times out, or routing persistently favors an earlier phase.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): under matched active human-control budgets, MoE-DAgger achieves 84.0% task success on Green and 78.0% on Red, exceeding phase-unaware filtered entropy by 22 percentage points on Green and 26 points on Red, with no observed collisions in 50 rollouts per task. On 50 shared intervention-free traces per task, 83.3% and 80.0% of its first proposals fall on failed rollouts within predefined failure windows when 15 and 25 traces are selected, compared with 70.0%/72.0% for temporal action-chunk disagreement and 63.3%/60.0% for ensemble disagreement.

title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
why: A-type hierarchical humanoid navigation harness: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum VLA for local motion-token prediction, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution are coordinated asynchronously with progress and arrival feedback so long-horizon language instructions can run across successive destinations.
mechanism: LHNav organizes long-horizon language-conditioned humanoid navigation into three complementary roles at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. An asynchronous system uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. A physics-grounded data engine trains the Cerebellum to track motion references along collision-aware routes and pairs the resulting demonstrations with rendered visual observations, so task planning can proceed alongside continuous movement.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): in simulation, the navigation VLA outperforms OmniNav and DualVLN in single-goal success and motion smoothness, with fewer collisions and falls (numeric tables beyond abstract unread). Using a VLA trained only on single-goal demonstrations, LHNav achieves a 75.56% success rate on long-horizon navigation tasks. Deployment on the Unitree G1 is reported for single-goal navigation and zero-shot long-horizon execution in real-world environments, including layouts with repositioned objects.

title: RoboWits: Unexpected Challenges for Robotic Creative Problem Solving
why: Update of the known RoboWits bimanual reasoning/tool-use benchmark: v2 changes the mutation-set size and adds a zero-shot frontier-VLM policy comparison, including a new GPT-6 Astra result that stronger foundation models alone do not close the robustness gap on mutated tasks.
mechanism: v2 keeps the multi-agent task-generation pipeline and the 30 seed tasks, but revises the mutated-task set from 208 (v1) to 200 and adds a zero-shot policy built on a frontier VLM to the benchmarked set (previously popular robot policies, pre-trained VLAs, and oracle-state planners). The new experiment reports that a GPT-6 Astra zero-shot policy outperforms all fine-tuned VLAs yet still loses about a fifth of its success on mutated tasks.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abstract): 30 seed tasks and 200 mutated tasks with graded difficulty across geometry, material, and assembly-based reasoning. Pre-trained VLAs show preliminary success on seed tasks after fine-tuning but struggle on mutated tasks. A zero-shot policy built on GPT-6 Astra outperforms all fine-tuned VLAs, yet still loses about a fifth of its success on mutated tasks. (v1 abs said 208 mutated tasks and did not include the frontier-VLM zero-shot comparison.)
